name: Gabon
tagline: Elephants on the beach at Loango
summary: Eighty-eight per cent forest, thirteen national parks covering eleven per cent of the country, and at Loango forest elephant, buffalo and hippo come out onto an Atlantic beach — the only place on earth where that happens.
when: The long dry season, May to September. Whales are offshore from July to September; turtles nest from November.

entries.caption: Loango
entries.description: Forest elephant and buffalo walking out of the trees onto the Atlantic sand.
entries.subject: forest elephants on the beach at Loango National Park

entries.caption: Eighty-Eight Per Cent Forest
entries.description: One of the most forested countries on earth, and eleven per cent of it in national parks.
entries.subject: unbroken rainforest running down to a lagoon in Gabon

entries.caption: Lowland Gorillas and Mandrills
entries.description: Habituated gorillas at Loango, and mandrill hordes at Lope that run to hundreds.
entries.subject: a mandrill with a bright face in Lope forest

entries.caption: Forest and Savanna at Lope
entries.description: Where the forest meets the last of the Ogooue savanna, with elephant and buffalo in both.
entries.subject: the forest edge meeting open savanna at Lope

entries.caption: The Chaillu Massif
entries.description: 1,575 metres at Mont Iboundji, forested to the top, in the middle of the country.
entries.subject: the forested Chaillu massif under cloud

entries.caption: Kongou and Mingouli
entries.description: Kongou on the Ivindo — three kilometres wide in flood, in the middle of rainforest.
entries.subject: the wide Kongou falls spread across rainforest on the Ivindo

entries.caption: The Ogooue and the Ivindo
entries.description: The Ogooue drains almost the whole country; the Ivindo runs through Ivindo National Park.
entries.subject: the Ogooue river running broad between forested banks

entries.caption: Eight Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Empty beaches with forest behind them, humpbacks offshore, and leatherbacks nesting.
entries.subject: an empty Atlantic beach backed by rainforest in Gabon

entries.caption: Congo Basin Forest
entries.description: Lope has one of the longest continuous records of forest-savanna change anywhere.
entries.subject: buttressed rainforest trees and understorey at Lope

entries.caption: Whales, Turtles and Surf
entries.description: Humpbacks from July, leatherbacks from November, and a beach nobody else is on.
entries.subject: a humpback whale breaching off the Gabonese coast

entries.caption: Bwiti
entries.description: An initiatory religion built around iboga, and the ceremonies run all night to harp and drum.
entries.subject: a Bwiti ceremony at night with harp and torches

entries.caption: Fang, Punu, Myene and the Baka
entries.description: Fang across the north, Punu in the south, and Baka forest people in the interior.
entries.subject: a Punu white-faced mask with carved coiffure

entries.caption: Nyembwe and Smoked Fish
entries.description: Chicken in palm nut nyembwe sauce, and river fish smoked over a slow fire.
entries.subject: a dish of poulet nyembwe with cassava

entries.caption: The Bwiti Night
entries.description: Ngombi harp, mouth bow and dancing until dawn, and it is a religion rather than a show.
entries.subject: musicians playing the ngombi harp at a night ceremony

entries.caption: Masks and Ngombi Harps
entries.description: Punu white-faced masks, Fang reliquary figures, and the carved harps of Bwiti.
entries.subject: a carved Fang reliquary guardian figure

entries.caption: Lope's Rock Art
entries.description: Engravings on the Ogooue at Lope, and Iron Age sites going back two and a half thousand years.
entries.subject: rock engravings on granite beside the Ogooue at Lope

entries.caption: Lope-Okanda, and Ivindo
entries.description: Two World Heritage sites: the forest-savanna mosaic, and the falls on the Ivindo.
entries.subject: the forest-savanna boundary landscape at Lope-Okanda

entries.caption: Libreville and Port-Gentil
entries.description: An Atlantic capital, and an oil town on an island at the Ogooue delta.
entries.subject: the seafront boulevard and buildings of Libreville

entries.caption: Colonial and Contemporary
entries.description: French colonial along the coast, and Libreville's newer buildings behind it.
entries.subject: a colonial-era building beside modern blocks in Libreville

entries.caption: Grilled Fish on the Sand
entries.description: The Libreville beach restaurants at the weekend, and the fish landed that morning.
entries.subject: grilled fish being served at a beach restaurant in Libreville

entries.caption: Elephants From a Boat
entries.description: Loango's lagoon puts you at eye level with elephant and buffalo, safely, from the water.
entries.subject: a boat on Loango lagoon with elephants on the far bank

entries.caption: Kayak, Trek and Boat
entries.description: Lagoon kayaking at Loango, forest trekking at Ivindo, and the train through Lope.
entries.subject: kayakers on the Loango lagoon at first light

entries.caption: A Handful, and Good
entries.description: Loango and Lope have real lodges, and the rest of the parks are camping.
entries.subject: a lodge deck overlooking the lagoon at Loango

entries.caption: Thirteen Parks in One Decision
entries.description: Gabon created all thirteen national parks in 2002, on one day, covering eleven per cent of the country.
entries.subject: a park boundary sign at the edge of Gabonese rainforest

entries.caption: Forest Meeting Ocean
entries.description: Loango at low sun, when the elephants come out and the beach is empty in both directions.
entries.subject: elephants crossing an empty beach with forest behind at sunset

entries.caption: The Trans-Gabonais
entries.description: The railway from Libreville to Franceville, straight through Lope, overnight.
entries.subject: the Trans-Gabonais railway running through rainforest

entries.caption: Why Gabon
entries.description: The only place in the world where forest elephants walk out onto an ocean beach.
entries.subject: a forest elephant standing on Atlantic sand at Loango
